faqs.question: What are TCCA chlorine tablets and how do they work in swimming pools?
faqs.answer: TCCA (Trichloroisocyanuric Acid) chlorine tablets are slow-dissolving, stabilized chlorine sanitisers used to maintain free chlorine residual in swimming pools. Each 200g tablet contains 90% available chlorine and built-in cyanuric acid stabiliser. When placed in an automatic feeder, skimmer basket, or floating dispenser, the tablet slowly dissolves over 3–7 days, releasing hypochlorous acid (the active biocide) that kills bacteria, viruses, and algae. Unlike unstabilised chlorine (sodium hypochlorite, calcium hypochlorite), TCCA's cyanuric acid protects the chlorine from UV degradation — essential in Oman's intense sunlight where unprotected chlorine can be destroyed within 2–4 hours.

faqs.question: How many chlorine tablets are needed for a swimming pool in Oman?
faqs.answer: For a typical residential pool in Oman (40,000–60,000 litres), 2–3 TCCA 200g tablets per week in a floating feeder or automatic feeder is the starting dose. The correct dose depends on pool volume, bather load, temperature, and sunlight exposure. In Oman's summer (ambient temperature 40–48°C), water temperature often reaches 35–40°C, which dramatically increases chlorine demand — you may need to increase to 3–4 tablets per week or add sodium hypochlorite for supplementary shock treatment. Always test free chlorine residual and maintain between 1.0–3.0 mg/L. For hotel or commercial pools with heavy bather loads, automatic dosing systems with online chlorine monitoring are recommended.

faqs.question: Why are stabilized chlorine tablets better than liquid bleach for outdoor pools in Oman?
faqs.answer: Oman's UV index regularly reaches 10–11 during summer months — among the highest in the world. At these UV levels, unstabilised chlorine (sodium hypochlorite or calcium hypochlorite without cyanuric acid) degrades within 2–4 hours of exposure, meaning a morning chlorine dose may be almost completely gone by afternoon. TCCA chlorine tablets contain cyanuric acid (CYA) stabiliser built into the chemical structure, extending effective chlorine residual to 3–7 days even in full sunlight. This makes TCCA tablets far more practical for outdoor pools in Oman — reducing dosing frequency, lowering chemical cost, and maintaining consistent protection between weekly maintenance visits.

faqs.question: How should chlorine tablets be stored safely in Oman's hot climate?
faqs.answer: TCCA chlorine tablets must be stored in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight and heat. In Oman's summer, outdoor storage temperatures can exceed 60°C in direct sun, which can cause rapid decomposition, chlorine gas release, and fire risk if TCCA comes into contact with moisture or organic materials. title: Calcium Hypochlorite Granules
description: Fast-dissolving granular chlorine for quick pool sanitization and shock treatment.

details.longDescription:
Calcium hypochlorite granules (cal-hypo, CAS 7778-54-3) carry 65–70% available chlorine and dissolve in 2–4 hours, giving a pH of 11–12 in solution. Global Chemicals LLC supplies them from stock in Muscat in 1 kg, 5 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg packs to hotels, resorts, public pools, pool-maintenance companies and residential users across Oman. Because cal-hypo contains no cyanuric acid, it is the correct shock chemical: TCCA and dichlor raise the stabiliser level with every dose, cal-hypo does not.

Shocking a pool. The shock dose is 150–300 g per 10,000 litres, which raises free chlorine by roughly 10–20 mg/L; use the higher end after algae, heavy bather loads, rain or a long closure, and dose to at least ten times the combined-chlorine reading when the aim is breakpoint chlorination to destroy chloramines, the cause of red eyes and the chlorine smell. Pre-dissolve the granules in a clean plastic bucket of pool water, stir, let the insoluble residue settle, and pour the clear liquid around the pool in the evening with the pump running; never broadcast granules onto a vinyl or dark-coloured surface, which they bleach. Keep bathers out until free chlorine falls below 5 mg/L. Oman's hotel pools, which see hundreds of bathers a day in season, shock weekly or twice weekly; residential pools after storms, parties and visible algae.

Side effects to manage: each shock adds calcium hardness and raises pH, so a cal-hypo-maintained pool needs periodic acid for pH and dilution when hardness passes about 400 mg/L; low-alkalinity water may cloud briefly after dosing. It is also the chemical for clearing cloudy water, opening and closing pools, and emergency disinfection of tanks and lines.

Handling and storage: calcium hypochlorite is an oxidiser (UN 2880, Class 5.1) that reacts violently with acids, TCCA, ammonia, fuels and organic matter. Store it sealed, cool, dry and apart from every other chemical; never add water to the product, always product to water; wear gloves, goggles and a dust mask. Every pack carries a GHS safety data sheet and certificate of analysis giving available chlorine.

details.longDescription:

It is the professional sanitiser for pools on automatic dosing: ORP controllers, peristaltic and diaphragm pumps and wall-mounted dispensers all meter it directly from the container, it disperses instantly with no undissolved residue, and it adds neither calcium hardness nor cyanuric acid, so a pool on liquid chlorine does not drift the way cal-hypo and tablet pools do. Each litre of 12% product raises free chlorine in 10,000 litres by about 12 mg/L: a shock dose is 0.8–1.5 L per 10,000 litres, and routine daily top-up is a fraction of that, set by the controller to hold 1–3 mg/L free chlorine. Because the solution is strongly alkaline, a liquid-chlorine pool needs regular acid to hold pH 7.2–7.6, which is why most dosing systems pair a hypochlorite pump with an acid pump.

Strength and storage. Hypochlorite loses available chlorine every day, and heat and sunlight speed the loss: a 12–15% product can lose a third of its strength in a month in an unshaded Omani plant room in summer. Buy quantities you will use within weeks, store containers closed in the shade or indoors, keep them off hot floors, and check the assay on the certificate against the date. Our stock turns over continuously and each delivery carries its assay certificate.

Handling: sodium hypochlorite is corrosive to eyes and skin and releases chlorine gas on contact with acid. Store it apart from acids and from calcium hypochlorite and TCCA, never mix chlorine products, use chemical-resistant pumps and lines, and wear gloves, goggles and a face shield. A GHS safety data sheet ships with every delivery.

title: Sodium Bi Sulphite Liquid
description: Liquid dechlorination agent for reducing excess chlorine levels in pools.

details.longDescription:
Liquid sodium bisulphite for pools (NaHSO3, CAS 7631-90-5) is a 38–40% solution, pH 3.5–5.0, supplied by Global Chemicals LLC from stock in Muscat in 5 L, 20 L and 60 L containers to hotels, resorts, water parks and pool-service companies across Oman. It is the chlorine neutraliser: a reducing agent that converts free chlorine to chloride within 15–30 minutes, bringing an over-chlorinated pool back to a swimmable level without waiting days for the sun to do it.

When to use it. After a shock treatment, when free chlorine is still above 5 mg/L and bathers are waiting; after a dosing-pump fault or a mis-measured dose; before draining a pool, spa or water-park feature to a drain or soakaway, where chlorinated water is not permitted; before adding chemicals that chlorine would destroy; and when chlorine is high enough to bleach swimwear, irritate eyes or corrode handrails and pump seals. The working rate is 100 mL per 10,000 litres for each 1 mg/L of free chlorine to be removed, which includes a safety margin over the stoichiometric quantity; dose with the pump running, wait 30 minutes and retest, adding a second smaller dose if needed. Dose in steps, because an overdose takes the chlorine to zero, drops the ORP reading, consumes dissolved oxygen and leaves the pool unprotected until chlorine is restored.

Side effects: the solution is acidic and will lower pH a little, so check pH and alkalinity after a large dose; it can also give a faint sulphur-dioxide smell while it reacts. It is compatible with all chlorine types, bromine and ozone systems. For plant-scale dechlorination ahead of reverse-osmosis membranes, see our water-treatment sodium bisulphite page.

Storage and handling: sodium bisulphite oxidises slowly in air and loses strength, so keep containers sealed, cool and shaded and use within a few months; it releases sulphur dioxide on contact with acid or chlorine, so store it apart from both. Wear gloves and goggles and handle it in a ventilated area. Every container carries a GHS safety data sheet and certificate of analysis giving assay.

Dosing. Dissolve the powder in a bucket of pool water and pour the solution around the pool with the pump running. Work in steps rather than one large dose: an overdose drives chlorine and ORP to zero and leaves the water unprotected until chlorine is re-established. The reaction lowers pH slightly, so check pH and alkalinity afterwards.

Uses: reopening a pool after shock treatment, correcting over-chlorination from a pump or controller fault, neutralising water before drain-down to a drain or garden, protecting liners, handrails and seals from sustained high chlorine, and resetting water chemistry before treatments that chlorine would break down. For continuous dechlorination in water-treatment plants and reverse-osmosis pre-treatment, see the water-treatment sodium bisulphite page.

Storage and handling: keep bags sealed and dry; the powder absorbs moisture and oxidises slowly to sulphate if left open, and it smells of sulphur dioxide. Store it away from acids and from chlorine products, which release sulphur dioxide on contact. Wear gloves, goggles and a dust mask when weighing. title: Trichloroisocyanuric Acid Tablet
description: Stabilized chlorine tablets with built-in cyanuric acid for UV protection.

details.longDescription:

They are the maintenance chlorine for outdoor pools in Oman because each tablet carries its own cyanuric acid, which shields the chlorine from sunlight; unstabilised chlorine in an exposed pool can lose most of its residual in a summer afternoon, stabilised chlorine lasts days.

Choosing the size. The 20 g tablets go in a floating dispenser or the skimmer basket of residential and villa pools, dissolving over three to four days; the 200 g tablets go in automatic erosion feeders on hotel, club and compound pools and last five to seven days (see the jumbo 3-inch page for large feeders). The usual rate is 1–3 tablets per 10,000 litres per week, adjusted to hold 1–3 mg/L free chlorine in the hot season. What to watch. Each tablet adds cyanuric acid, and once it passes about 80 mg/L the stabiliser slows chlorine so much that algae can grow with a normal reading; test it monthly, keep it at 30–50 mg/L and dilute with fresh water when it climbs. TCCA is acidic (pH 2.8–3.2 in solution), so a tablet-fed pool needs sodium bicarbonate or soda ash to hold pH 7.2–7.6 and alkalinity 80–120 mg/L. For shock treatment use unstabilised calcium hypochlorite, not more tablets. Skimmer dosing stops when the pump stops and gives an acidic, high-chlorine slug on restart, so a floater or feeder is better.

Handling and storage: TCCA is an oxidiser (UN 2468, Class 5.1). Never mix it with calcium hypochlorite, acids, ammonia or any other pool chemical, in a bucket or a feeder, because the mixture can ignite or release chlorine gas; keep buckets sealed, dry, cool and out of the sun, away from fuels and metals, and wear gloves and goggles. title: Chlorine Powder
description: Powdered chlorine for rapid pool treatment and shock applications.

details.longDescription:
Chlorine powder for pools is calcium hypochlorite (CAS 7778-54-3) milled to a fine powder, with 65–70% available chlorine, pH 11–12 in solution and no cyanuric acid stabiliser. Global Chemicals LLC supplies it from stock in Muscat in 500 g, 1 kg, 5 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg packs to pool-maintenance companies, hotels, villa compounds and residential pool owners across Oman. It is the same chemistry as our calcium hypochlorite granules; the powder dissolves fastest and is dosed by weight, while the granules suit users who want less dust and a slower release.

Dosing by weight. With a 65% product, 15 g per 10,000 litres raises free chlorine by 1 mg/L, so the shock dose of 150–300 g per 10,000 litres gives a 10–20 mg/L rise; weigh the dose from the pool volume and the chlorine reading rather than guessing. Pre-dissolve the powder in a clean plastic bucket of pool water, stir, let any residue settle, and pour the clear solution around the pool in the evening with the pump running so sunlight does not burn off the chlorine before it works. Never pour powder straight into a skimmer or a feeder that has held TCCA, and never broadcast it onto a liner or a dark surface, which it bleaches.

What it is for: the weekly or twice-weekly shock programme of hotel and compound pools, breakpoint chlorination to destroy chloramines (dose at least ten times the combined-chlorine reading), rapid killing of green algae, clearing cloudy water, super-chlorination after parties, rain or heavy use, opening and closing pools, and emergency disinfection of tanks and lines. Because it carries no stabiliser it does not raise cyanuric acid, which stabilised tablets do; because it carries calcium, it raises hardness a little with each dose, which liquid chlorine does not.

Handling and storage: calcium hypochlorite is an oxidiser (UN 2880, Class 5.1) that reacts violently with acids, TCCA, ammonia, fuels and organic matter, and the fine powder is an eye and respiratory irritant. Store it sealed, cool, dry and apart from every other chemical, add product to water and never water to product, and wear gloves, goggles and a dust mask. Every pack carries a GHS safety data sheet and certificate of analysis giving available chlorine.
